_comment: Curated A4 measurement data. Hand-authored from the service manuals.
There are no test points on this board. Table 6-5 lists no TP designator, the
locator drawing shows none, and none of the three schematic sheets carries a
test point legend -- which is what a backplane looks like. So 'testpoints' is
deliberately an empty list, and everything measurable is a probe point,
identified by connector and pin.
Two groups of them, and they are read very differently.
1. The transformer secondaries on J13. Schematic sheet 2 prints a voltage
beside every winding and states its conditions outright: 'SECONDARY
VOLTAGES ASSUME PRIMARY IS 122V, 60Hz. SECONDARY VOLTAGES REPRESENT OPEN
CIRCUIT MEASUREMENT.' Sheet 3 prints J13's pin map. Putting the two
together gives a published expected value at a named pin pair, which is
the only place in the manuals that exists for this board. No tolerance is
published for any of them, and none is invented here: a reading taken in
circuit is loaded and will sit several per cent low, and the values scale
with the line, so an invented +-10% band would fail a good transformer.
The nominal is the printed number and the condition says what it means.
2. The ac line points on sheet 1. These have no published value at all --
they are whatever the supply is -- so they carry noPublishedValue and
exist to say where the line is, which is the question that matters when
the instrument is dead. Every one of them is at line potential.
The winding-to-signal mapping on J13 was traced on sheet 2 and then checked
against three independent things: the wire colours P13 prints beside each pin
(VI/RED, GN/BLK, GN/BRN, OR/BLK, BR/BLK), the centre tap, which only the
12.9 V + 12.9 V pair has and only the 12 AC group needs, and the rails A19
makes from them. That last check is the strongest: 12.9-0-12.9 V ac rectifies
to about 18 V, which is the +/-12VUR figure the A19 dataset derived from its
own 25 V reservoir capacitors; 8.3 V ac gives about 11.7 V peak against A19's
derived +5VUR of ~8.5 V on 16 V parts; 39.5 V ac gives about 56 V against a
100 V C3; and 82.9 V ac gives about 117 V against a 160 V C1. All four agree.
'source' on every value says where it came from. Nothing here is inferred
into a nominal.
rails is empty for the same reason testpoints is: this board has none of its
own. The routing paths it does have are described in data/a4.reference.json
under railCircuits, which assemble.py only emits for rails declared here --
so they are declared here with no com, because there is no test point on this
assembly for a meter's low lead to go to.

AC.label: AC line input and line select

DIGITAL.label: Digital secondaries and rails to A19

FAN.label: 24 V fan supply and current sense

probePoints.label: J13 pin 1 to pin 2 (5 AC 1 / 5 AC 2)
probePoints.condition: Instrument on, line-select switches correct for the supply. The printed figure is an open-circuit value at a 122 V 60 Hz primary; measured in circuit with A19 fitted it will read several per cent lower, and it scales with the line.
probePoints.source: Schematic sheet 2 (winding S2-12) and sheet 3 (J13 pin map)
probePoints.note: The secondary A19 makes the +5 V logic rail from — the rail the CPU runs on, so this is the first measurement to take on an instrument that will not boot. 8.3 V ac rectifies and filters to about 11.7 V peak, which is A19's +5VUR on its 16 V reservoir capacitors C12/C13. Dead here with the line present at J11 means the transformer or its primary; present here and dead at J41 means this board's track between the two, which is the only thing between them.

probePoints.label: J13 pin 4 to pin 5 (75 AC 1 / 75 AC 2)
probePoints.condition: Instrument on, line-select switches correct for the supply. Open-circuit value at a 122 V 60 Hz primary; see the caveat on sheet 2's conditions.
probePoints.source: Schematic sheet 2 (winding S2-13) and sheet 3 (J13 pin map)
probePoints.note: The highest voltage on this connector and the source of A19's +75 V display supply — about 117 V peak behind A19's 160 V reservoir C1. Treat J13 as a hazardous connector for this pair alone.

probePoints.label: J13 pin 6 to pin 7 (35 AC 1 / 35 AC 2)
probePoints.condition: Instrument on, line-select switches correct for the supply. Open-circuit value at a 122 V 60 Hz primary.
probePoints.source: Schematic sheet 2 (winding S1-14) and sheet 3 (J13 pin map)
probePoints.note: Feeds A19's +35 V display supply, about 56 V peak behind its 100 V reservoir C3.

probePoints.label: J13 pin 8 to pin 9 (12 AC 1 to the centre tap)
probePoints.condition: Instrument on, line-select switches correct for the supply. Open-circuit value at a 122 V 60 Hz primary.
probePoints.source: Schematic sheet 2 (winding S1-11) and sheet 3 (J13 pin map)
probePoints.note: Half of the centre-tapped winding that makes A19's ±12 V pair — and with it the ±12V FAN lines that run both chassis fans through R2 and R3 on this board. Check it against pin 9 to pin 10: the two halves should read the same, and a difference points at the transformer rather than at anything here.

probePoints.label: J13 pin 9 to pin 10 (centre tap to 12 AC 2)
probePoints.condition: Instrument on, line-select switches correct for the supply. Open-circuit value at a 122 V 60 Hz primary.
probePoints.source: Schematic sheet 2 (winding S1-11) and sheet 3 (J13 pin map)
probePoints.note: The other half of the centre-tapped 12 V winding. Pin 9 is 12 AC CT, which is the only centre tap on this connector and the reference for both halves.

probePoints.label: J13 pin 8 to pin 10 (12 AC 1 to 12 AC 2, across the whole winding)
probePoints.condition: Instrument on, line-select switches correct for the supply. Open-circuit value at a 122 V 60 Hz primary.
probePoints.source: Derived: the sum of the two 12.9 V halves sheet 2 prints for winding S1-11
probePoints.note: Derived rather than printed — sheet 2 gives the two halves and not the total. Worth taking because it is the quickest check that the centre tap is where it should be: a total that is right while one half is wrong means the tap connection, not the winding.

probePoints.label: J31 pin 1 to pin 2 (LINE / NEUT), ahead of the power switch
probePoints.condition: Line cord plugged in. The instrument does NOT have to be switched on — SW1 is downstream of this point.
probePoints.note: Where the ac line arrives on the board, from the rear-panel receptacle through the line filter FL1 and P31, none of which is on this assembly. No expected value is published because there is none to publish: it is whatever the supply is. Live whenever the cord is in, which is the fact worth carrying — the front-panel power switch does not isolate this point, this track, or SW1 itself.

probePoints.label: F1, downstream side, to neutral
probePoints.condition: Line cord plugged in and the instrument switched on.
probePoints.note: The line after the switch and the fuse. Present here with the instrument dead puts the fault beyond F1 — the line-select switches, J11, or the transformer. Absent here with the line present at J31 means SW1 or F1. Before fitting a second fuse read §2-61 and check RV2: A18's triac circuit blows F1 deliberately when the line-select switches are set for the wrong supply, and a varistor that has failed short blows it every time.

probePoints.label: J11, the switched line out to the transformer primary
probePoints.condition: Line cord plugged in and the instrument switched on. Which pins are live depends on the line-select switches.
probePoints.note: The last point on this board before the transformer. Sheet 1 sends eight lines here — 108A, 122A, 8A, 0A, 108B, 122B, 8B, 0B — plus SHIELD, and sheet 2 shows them arriving on P11 at the primary taps: pin 1 122A, 2 108A, 4 8A, 5 0A, 7 122B, 8 108B, 10 8B, 11 0B, 12 EARTH. Which pair carries the line is the whole function of SW2, SW3 and SW4, so this is also where a line-select fault is confirmed: compare the live pins against sheet 1's switch table for the setting the switches are actually in. Silkscreened WARNING HIGH VOLTAGE.

probePoints.label: Across R2 (FAN1 current sense)
probePoints.condition: Instrument on, fan 1 running, J51 connected.
probePoints.note: The analog signal FAN1 is the drop across this 2 Ω resistor, and §2-45 says the CPU's fan monitor subtracts FAN1 from FAN2 and raises FANINT* if the difference leaves a window. The manuals tabulate no voltage for it, so none is given here. What it is good for is a comparison rather than an absolute: measure across R2 and across R3 and expect them to match, because that is the only thing the monitor actually judges. A fan fault reported with both fans visibly turning is a reason to look at R2, R3 and their connectors before the fans.

probePoints.label: Across R3 (FAN2 current sense)
probePoints.condition: Instrument on, fan 2 running, J52 connected.
probePoints.note: The companion to R2, generating FAN2. Same reading, same comparison; see the note on R2.
